1.w: Do not boast about tomorrow; for you do not know what a day may bring forth.

2.w: Let another praise you, and not your own mouth; someone else, and not your own lips.

3.w: A stone is heavy and sand is weighty, but vexation by a fool is more burdensome than the two of them.

4.w: Wrath is cruel and anger is overwhelming, but who can stand before jealousy?

5.w: Better is open rebuke than hidden love.

6.w: Faithful are the wounds of a friend, but the kisses of an enemy are excessive.

7.w: The one whose appetite is satisfied loathes honey, but to the hungry mouth every bitter thing is sweet.

8.w: Like a bird that wanders from its nest, so is a person who wanders from his home.

9.w: Ointment and incense make the heart rejoice, likewise the sweetness of one’s friend from sincere counsel.

10.w: Do not forsake your friend and your father’s friend, and do not enter your brother’s house in the day of your disaster; a neighbor nearby is better than a brother far away.

11.w: Be wise, my son, and make my heart glad, so that I may answer anyone who taunts me.

12.w: A shrewd person saw danger—he hid himself; the naive passed right on by — they had to pay for it.

13.w: Take a man’s garment when he has given security for a stranger, and hold him in pledge on behalf of a stranger.

14.w: If someone blesses his neighbor with a loud voice early in the morning, it will be counted as a curse to him.

15.w: A continual dripping on a rainy day— a contentious wife makes herself like that.

16.w: Whoever contains her has contained the wind or can grasp oil with his right hand.

17.w: As iron sharpens iron, so a person sharpens his friend.

18.w: The one who tends a fig tree will eat its fruit, and whoever takes care of his master will be honored.

19.w: As in water the face is reflected as a face, so a person’s heart reflects the person.

20.w: As Death and Destruction are never satisfied, so the eyes of a person are never satisfied.

21.w: As the crucible is for silver and the furnace is for gold, so a person must put his praise to the test.

22.w: If you should pound the fool in the mortar among the grain with the pestle, his foolishness would not depart from him.

23.w: Pay careful attention to the condition of your flocks, set your mind on your herds,

24.w: for riches do not last forever, nor does a crown last from generation to generation.

25.w: When the hay is removed and new grass appears, and the grass from the hills is gathered in,

26.w: the lambs will be for your clothing, and the goats will be for the price of a field.

27.w: And there will be enough goat’s milk for your food, for the food of your household, and for the sustenance of your servant girls.
